title.narrative: AAP 2024: Action Document for Fighting Organised Crime (AD3)

description.narrative: The overall objective of the action is the increased effectiveness of efforts to combat organised crime, illicit trafficking in all its forms, smuggling and disrupting criminal networks along main trafficking routes. This objective will be pursued mainly through the Global Illicit Flows Programme, an umbrella programme under which the support to combating environmental crime, trafficking by sea, and SALW proliferation will be delivered.Component 1: Container Control Programme (CCP) (EUR 6 million): The specific objective of this component is to support the disruption of illicit trafficking via maritime containers, through strengthening capacities for identifying and searching suspicious containers, exchanging information and intelligence, and improving interdiction capacities in major international seaports.Component 2: Global Organised Crime Threat Assessment (GLOCTA) (EUR 10 million): The specific objective of this component is to build global capacity for organized crime analysis and threat assessment, notably by supporting the implementation of relevant EMPACT Operational Actions, helping identify High Value Targets; building capacities in criminal intelligence analysis within selected law enforcement agencies; supporting the preparation of the flagship publication `Global Organized Crime Index¿; and building a trans-regional network of relevant actors to enhance research on illicit flows and develop evidence-based policy recommendations. Component 3: Responsible Use of Artificial Intelligence in Law Enforcement (EUR 2 million): The specific objective of this component is to promote and support the responsible use of artificial intelligence (AI) in law enforcement by accompanying globally the implementation of the Toolkit for Responsible Artificial Intelligence Innovation in Law Enforcement in a way that is lawful, responsible and human rights compliant.Component 4: SIRIUS (EUR 3.5 million): The specific objective of this component is to support the cross-border exchange of digital evidence between the EU and eligible third parties and to build capacity for third party states to enable them to meet relevant standards for e-evidence exchange. All components will be implemented in full complementarity with bilateral and regional programmes and Common Foreign and Security Policy (CFSP) actions and in coordination with EU Delegations and relevant units in INTPA, NEAR and ENV.
